title: Payload contract enforcer and skeletonized decoder tests for structured outputs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
Build a lightweight enforcement harness (payload contract enforcer) that runs alongside the serving runtime and validates/experiments with structured outputs (JSON mode) during streaming, interleaved tool/function calls, and constrained decoding scenarios. The goal is to catch schema drift and decoding failures early, quantify failure modes, and validate fallback strategies before flipping to hard enforcement in production.

Background & motivation:
- We've observed intermittent structured-output regressions during streaming and when models interleave tool calls. These regressions manifest as truncated JSON, extra trailing tokens, or out-of-schema fields. Current detection is ad-hoc in clients and inconsistent across SDKs.
- Before enabling a strict "reject-on-violation" policy, we need repeatable tests and a staged rollout plan. This ticket creates the canonical harness and a small test-suite that can be used in canaries and CI.

Scope (what we will deliver):
1) A runtime-adjacent verifier process (non-blocking by default) that:
   - attaches to streaming responses and attempts incremental JSON reconstruction;
   - applies configured schemas (json-schema / OpenAPI-style) and a small set of guarded constraints (required fields, types, enum values);
   - records a structured violation event with minimal context (token offsets, partial payload snapshot, model & config).
2) Skeletonized constrained-decoder test cases that exercise common failure modes: partial emits, mid-stream toolcall injection, KV-cache cold-starts, and low-temperature sampling with quantized models.
3) Canary plan and rollout flags: observability-only for one week, then soft-fallback mode (repair attempts + best-effort tool re-invoke), then optional hard-reject gating per route.
4) Dashboard telemetry definitions and alert thresholds (schema_violation_rate, decoder_repair_rate, mean_time_to_repair).

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness integrated with streaming path in a feature-flagged way; can be enabled in staging and mirrored canaries.
- Test suite contains >= 12 deterministic scenarios covering at least 4 model variants and both streaming and non-streaming flows.
- Violation events are emitted to telemetry with schema: {timestamp, model, route, violation_type, snippet}.
- Canary run for 72 hours with observability-only mode shows stable baseline; documented rollback thresholds.

Test matrix (high level):
- TC-01: Complete well-formed JSON in single stream (should pass).
- TC-02: Truncated JSON due to mid-stream interruption (should record violation, attempt heuristic repair if soft-fallback enabled).
- TC-03: Interleaved tool call that emits partial JSON before tool invocation (simulate tool boundary tokens).
- TC-04: Extra unexpected field introduced by model ensemble (type mismatch detection).
- TC-05: Low-temperature sampling causing enumerated-field mismatch (should be flagged).
- TC-06: Quantized model (q4* family) with short context causing tokenization boundary splits (observe repair success rate).

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Enforcement vs availability: We will default to observability-only for initial rollout. Hard enforcement has customer impact where downstream consumers expect graceful degradation.
- Repair heuristics: Implement a conservative repair that closes open brackets and strips trailing garbage; do not attempt semantic re-generation in the first phase. Full auto-repair may be introduced later behind a rate-limited feature flag.
- Performance: Verifier will run in a separate thread/process to avoid adding token-latency to critical path. Telemetry will include sampling to bound cost.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy to staging; run the deterministic suite and validate telemetry emission.
2) Mirror 1% of controlled production routes with observability-only flag for 7 days.
3) Evaluate metrics; if schema_violation_rate < 0.05% AND decoder_repair_rate > 20% then enable soft-fallback for additional 7 days.
4) If soft-fallback causes no customer-facing errors (SLO unaffected), consider hard-reject on lower-risk routes.

Telemetry & alerts:
- Metrics: schema_violation_rate, constrained_decode_failure_rate, decoder_repair_rate, mean_time_to_repair, violations_by_route.
- Alerts: P1 if schema_violation_rate increases >3x baseline for >30m on any high-traffic route.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Payload+Contract+Enforcer+Design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345
- Example schema repo (internal drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/structured-output-schemas

Open questions / next steps:
- Should the verifier store raw token sequences for postmortem analysis? (privacy implications + storage cost) -> For now store only minimal snippets and token offsets.
- Define the canonical schema publishing workflow for customer teams (PMs/platform owners).

Risks:
- False positives could drive noisy alerts and erode trust; mitigated by observability-first rollouts and conservative constraints.
- Performance overhead if sampling not configured; mitigated by separate process and sampling defaults.
